description: Reading an offer: the reader reads the letter and the pay context, then submits notes on three clauses, two differences and two questions for a lawyer.

content.text: I read the letter, then what it is compared with.

input.summary: Lumen Example offers you the role of Senior Platform Engineer on a permanent contract, starting on 1 December 2026, for 4,500 EUR gross a month.

clauses.title: Trial period
clauses.quote: The trial period is four months, renewable once.
clauses.plain: For the first four months, you or the employer can end the contract quickly. The employer may renew it once; the letter does not say for how long.

clauses.title: Pay
clauses.quote: Your gross monthly salary will be 4,500 EUR, paid over twelve months.
clauses.plain: You are paid 4,500 EUR gross each month, twelve times a year. The letter names no bonus.

clauses.title: Non-compete
clauses.quote: For twelve months after you leave, you will not work for a competitor in France.
clauses.plain: For a year after you leave, you agree not to work for a company the employer calls a competitor, in France. The letter does not say whether you are paid during that year.

differences: The letter states 4,500 EUR gross a month; the posting stated 55,000 to 65,000 EUR a year.
You seek 60,000 to 70,000 EUR a year; the letter states a monthly figure only.
questions: Trial period: how long can the renewal last, and what notice applies during it?
Non-compete: is a payment owed for the twelve months, and which companies count as competitors?
